sections.content: Use *antes* de + infinitive to say that one action happened before another. When the main action is expressed with the pretérito perfecto, the perfect form shows the completed action, while antes de introduces the action that happened first. The infinitive does not change for the subject.

items.spanish: He lavado las manos antes de empezar.
items.english: I have washed my hands before starting.

items.spanish: Hemos preparado los ingredientes antes de cocinar.
items.english: We have prepared the ingredients before cooking.

items.spanish: Carlos ha cortado las verduras antes de empezar.
items.english: Carlos has cut the vegetables before starting.

items.spanish: Han lavado las manos antes de ponerse el delantal.
items.english: They have washed their hands before putting on the apron.

sections.content: The verb after *antes* de and *después* de stays in the infinitive: antes de *cocinar*, después de cocinar.
